sources.name: FRED: Brent crude oil spot price, monthly (US EIA series MCOILBRENTEU)

steps.title: 2014: oil above $100
text: In June 2014 Brent crude cost **$111.80** a barrel. That year the world's economies exported **$1.49 trillion** of crude oil.
The map shows each country's crude oil exports (CEPII BACI).

steps.title: The price collapses
text: By January 2016 Brent had fallen to **$30.70**. World crude oil exports fell to $808 billion in 2015 (−46%) and **$689 billion** in 2016, less than half their 2014 value.
The map shows the change from the year before.

steps.title: Oil exporters' earnings halve
text: Total goods exports fell **53%** in Saudi Arabia from 2014 to 2016 ($443 billion to $207 billion), 65% in Nigeria, 64% in Venezuela, 43% in Russia and 39% in Norway.
Switch to Log to see that the falls were similar in proportion, whatever the country's size.

steps.title: Venezuela's collapse
text: Countries that depended most on oil suffered most. Venezuela's real GDP shrank 6.2% in 2015 and **17.1%** in 2016.
World goods exports as a whole fell from $18.9 trillion in 2014 to $15.9 trillion in 2016 (−16%), in part because lower oil prices cut the value of trade.
